text.p: Syratech, a maker and distributor of tabletops and giftware, said Tuesday its net sales for January and February rose 63.8 percent from a year earlier, to $26.9 million from $16.4 million.

It said a significant portion of the sales increase came from businesses acquired in 1996. If the sales from those acquisitions were not considered, the sales increase would have been 39.2 percent, it said.

Syratech also announced that a special stockholder meeting has been scheduled for April 14 to vote on the proposed merger of the company with a corporation formed by the Thomas H. Lee Equity Fund III LP, a private investment firm based in Boston.
It said the record date for stockholders entitled to vote at the meeting was fixed at March 5.

Under the proposed merger, Syratech stockholders would receive $32 cash for each share held, or they may elect to retain up to 34.75 percent of their shares, subject to certain limitations, including proration.
